high.title: TSMC Hit by DRAM Shortage — $1B Worth of Apple Processors Stuck, iPhone 18 Supply Chain at Risk
high.summary: Industry sources report that TSMC (2330) is currently holding approximately USD $1 billion worth of Apple A20 Pro processors that cannot be shipped due to a severe DRAM shortage. The chips — manufactured using TSMC's cutting-edge 2nm (N2) process and assembled via Wafer-Level Multi-Chip Module (WMCM) packaging — are waiting on DRAM deliveries before final packaging and shipment can proceed. This bottleneck is directly impacting the production schedule for the iPhone 18 series, which is expected to launch in approximately six weeks. Apple primarily sources DRAM from Micron, with secondary suppliers SK Hynix and Samsung. While Apple and its assemblers expressed confidence in meeting initial launch demand, they warned that wait times for online orders could lengthen significantly if retail inventory depletes quickly. TSMC shares fell NT$40 to close at NT$2,365 on the news. This is a meaningful near-term risk for TSMC's revenue recognition timing and for the broader Apple supply chain. Investors should monitor DRAM supply developments and any official commentary from TSMC or Apple regarding production recovery timelines.

high.title: TSMC Achieves Next-Generation Technology Breakthrough — Opens "Post-Silicon" Era with MoS₂ Transistor
high.summary: Taiwan's National Science and Technology Council (NSTC) announced that TSMC (2330), in collaboration with National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University (NYCU), has successfully developed a high-performance single-layer Molybdenum Disulfide (MoS₂) top-gate transistor — a landmark achievement in extending semiconductor scaling beyond the limits of Moore's Law. The research has been published in the prestigious journal *Nature Electronics*, underscoring its scientific significance. Industry analysts note that as semiconductor nodes push below 1nm into the 0.7nm (A7 / CFET) generation, transitioning to new two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor materials such as MoS₂ becomes essential. Major equipment makers including Applied Materials, ASML, AIXTRON, ASM International, and Lam Research are all actively investing in R&D aligned with MoS₂ process requirements. For investors, this breakthrough reinforces TSMC's long-term technology leadership and its strategic positioning well into the next decade. While near-term revenue impact is limited, this development supports a structurally bullish view on TSMC's competitive moat against Samsung and Intel Foundry over a 5–10 year horizon.

high.title: US July Non-Farm Payrolls Miss Expectations, Reducing Fed Rate Hike Risk — US Stocks Close Higher
high.summary: US July non-farm payrolls came in significantly below analyst expectations, with job numbers unexpectedly declining. The weaker-than-anticipated labor data triggered a notable selloff in the US dollar and materially reduced market concerns over further Federal Reserve rate hikes. US equities responded positively: the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained +0.28% to close at 54,036.93; the S&P 500 rose +0.62% to 7,757.64; the Nasdaq surged +1.30% to 26,690.62; and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped +2.56% to 12,356.789 — a notably strong signal for Taiwan's tech-heavy market.

high.title: Taiwan Stock Market: Domestic Institutional Conflict — Investment Trusts Sell, State Banks Buy; Index Rebounds 1,106 Points for the Week, Breaking Out of July Slump
high.summary: Taiwan's equity market posted a weekly gain of 1,106 points (+2.5%), recovering from July's weakness, with the TAIEX closing at 44,225 on Friday — down 170 points on the day but holding above the critical 44,000 level. The session saw notable institutional divergence: foreign investors (FINI) reversed course to net sell NT$40.71 billion, investment trust funds (投信) unexpectedly ended a 32-session consecutive buying streak to net sell NT$1.2 billion, while state-owned banks stepped in with NT$11.57 billion in support purchases. TSMC was selectively bought by foreign investors at NT$1.52 billion, even as they offloaded names including Winbond, Yageo, Delta Electronics, Accton, and UMC.

medium.title: Barron's Decodes Cloud Giants' Earnings — Strong Monetization Eases AI Capex Concerns, Benefiting Taiwan AI Supply Chain
medium.summary: Barron's analysis of Q2 earnings from Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet reveals that cloud service providers (CSPs) are increasingly efficient at converting revenue into profit — with combined incremental cloud margins jumping from 33.8% to 50.9% year-over-year, meaning over $0.50 of every new dollar of cloud revenue now flows to operating profit. Combined annualized new cloud revenue from the three giants reached $56 billion in Q2. Institutional investors note that this data point helps rebuild market confidence following recent chip stock sell-offs driven by concerns over the ROI of AI infrastructure spending. Taiwan-based AI supply chain companies including TSMC, Hon Hai (2317), Quanta, and Wiwynn are seen as direct beneficiaries of sustained hyperscaler capex, and this earnings data supports continued strong demand for Taiwan's AI hardware ecosystem.

medium.title: King Slide (川湖) Posts Record Q2 EPS of NT$74.38, Becomes Taiwan's Third-Ever NT$10,000+ Stock
medium.summary: Server slide rail manufacturer King Slide (2059) reported a record Q2 net profit of NT$7.088 billion, with EPS of NT$74.38 — up 10.5x year-over-year — driven by surging AI server demand and penetration into major hyperscaler and ASIC server supply chains. First-half EPS reached NT$110.96, already surpassing full-year 2025 earnings. July revenue of NT$6.407 billion set another monthly record, up 3.5x year-over-year. The stock surged to NT$10,100, making King Slide only the third stock in Taiwan market history to exceed NT$10,000 per share. Gross margin reached a record 87.42% in Q2, exceeding even Nvidia's margin profile. A US Houston plant expansion is targeted for Q3 production ramp. This is a notable signal of AI-driven hardware demand strength in Taiwan's listed manufacturing sector.

medium.title: Adata Technology (Yicheng): Six-Month Profit Exceeds Past 20 Years Combined — Q2 EPS of NT$108.93 Sets Domestic Memory Industry Record
medium.summary: Memory module maker Adata Technology (5289) reported Q2 after-tax net income of NT$10.368 billion, a record high, up 90% quarter-on-quarter and surging more than 55-fold year-on-year. Q2 EPS reached NT$108.93 — the highest single-quarter EPS ever recorded in Taiwan's memory industry. For H1 2026, after-tax net income totalled NT$15.834 billion, up 29x year-on-year, with H1 EPS of NT$166.45. Notably, the company's H1 2026 profit alone exceeds its cumulative earnings from its founding in 2005 through 2025. The explosive growth is attributed to a memory super-cycle driven by AI server and edge computing demand, with tight supply-demand dynamics in both DRAM and NAND Flash. The company expects supply tightness to persist into H2, with DRAM remaining stable and NAND continuing to grow. AI system solutions revenue is projected to double year-on-year, with new projects involving partners including NVIDIA entering development phases. Shares hit the daily limit-up at NT$1,610. **Market implication:** Adata's outsized earnings reflect the broader AI-driven memory upcycle — relevant for fund managers assessing Taiwan's technology sector momentum and identifying potential re-rating candidates.

medium.title: Winbond Electronics: DRAM Supply-Demand to Tighten Further in 2027 — Board Approves NT$13.07 Billion Capex Budget
medium.summary: Winbond Electronics (2344) held an investor conference on August 6, with President Chen Pei-ming projecting that DRAM supply tightness will extend through 2027, with next year's supply-demand balance expected to be even tighter than 2026. Winbond's board simultaneously approved a NT$13.074 billion capital expenditure budget, to be deployed from August onward for production equipment, R&D, and facility upgrades. Management cited AI servers, data centers, and automotive demand as key drivers, noting that major international memory makers continue shifting capacity toward HBM, DDR5, and LPDDR5, rapidly shrinking supply of mature-node DRAM. Some customers have already initiated long-term supply agreement (LTA) discussions covering 2029–2030. The Kaohsiung fab is identified as Winbond's primary growth engine, with monthly capacity currently at ~15,000 wafers and expansion planned. **Market implication:** The significant capex commitment signals management confidence in a multi-year upcycle; investors should monitor capacity execution and margin trends as a gauge of Taiwan's memory sector investment cycle.

medium.title: Taiwan Stock Market Resilience Amid Korean Market Crash — Will TAIEX Break Below 40,000 Again?
medium.summary: Taiwan's equity market demonstrated notable resilience on August 6 as the Korean KOSPI plunged more than 5% intraday, dragging the TAIEX down over 500 points at the open before a swift recovery. The index ultimately closed down only 214 points, while the OTC small/mid-cap index bucked the trend with a nearly 2% gain — a constructive signal for broader market confidence. Moore Investment Advisory CIO Kuo Che-jung estimates the probability of TAIEX re-breaking below 40,000 points at less than 5%, characterizing the earlier dip below that level as a buying opportunity rather than a panic signal, and maintaining a year-end target of 50,000. On the memory side, SanDisk's latest earnings beat estimates (EPS NT$39.25 vs. consensus NT$34), with next-quarter guidance also above consensus, though shares fell 8% after-hours on a revenue outlook perceived as slightly below the most bullish market expectations. Passive components makers Murata and Taiyo Yuden raised guidance, supporting the view that AI server, automotive, and high-performance computing demand remains structurally intact. **Market implication:** The divergence between Taiwan and Korea underscores Taiwan's tech-driven resilience; fund managers should monitor memory and passive component names as near-term volatility may present entry points.

medium.title: U.S. Stocks Mostly Lower Ahead of July Jobs Report
medium.summary: U.S. equities retreated broadly on August 6 ahead of the July non-farm payrolls release, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 464 points (-0.85%) to 53,885 and the S&P 500 slipping 0.18% to 7,709. The Nasdaq edged down just 0.06%, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index outperformed, rising 0.33% to 12,048 — a positive read-through for Taiwan's semiconductor supply chain. **Market implication:** The jobs report outcome will be a key near-term catalyst for Fed rate expectations, USD/TWD dynamics, and foreign investor flows into Taiwan equities. A weaker-than-expected print could reinforce rate-cut expectations, potentially supportive for Taiwan life insurers' bond portfolios and foreign-held Taiwan tech stocks.

medium.title: Iran Proposes Banning U.S. and Israeli Vessels from Strait of Hormuz — Oil Prices Surge Over $3/barrel
medium.summary: An Iranian parliamentary committee is reviewing legislation that would ban U.S. and Israeli vessels from transiting the Strait of Hormuz, with penalties of up to one-fifth of cargo value for violations. The news drove WTI crude up 2.75% to $77.29/barrel and Brent up 3.83% to $82.49/barrel. **Market implication:** Sustained oil price elevation adds to global inflationary pressures, which could complicate the Fed's rate path and delay CBC easing in Taiwan. For Taiwan life insurers with significant overseas fixed-income and equity exposure, a risk-off environment driven by Middle East escalation warrants close monitoring of foreign exchange hedging costs and unrealized gains on overseas portfolios.

medium.title: Hon Hai and Lite-On Technology Among Four Stocks in Focus; Foreign Buying Provides Support
medium.summary:
Hon Hai (2317) posted record-breaking July revenue of NT$946.51 billion, up 15.1% month-on-month and 54.1% year-on-year, exceeding market expectations, driven by strong AI server and notebook PC demand. Institutional analysts maintain a positive outlook for Q3, forecasting high single-digit sequential revenue growth, with AI server cabinet shipments expected to double year-over-year in 2026. Hon Hai is also set to begin shipping CPO (Co-Packaged Optics) products in Q3, with approximately 10,000 units in H2 2026, scaling to 3–4x that volume in H1 2027, which should support margin expansion. Lite-On Technology (2301) also beat Q2 gross margin expectations, with Q3 revenue guided up 15–20% sequentially as next-generation GPU and ASIC power supply products ramp. Both stocks have attracted recent foreign investor buying, reinforcing positive near-term sentiment.

medium.title: Evergreen and Wan Hai Post Strong July Revenues on Peak Season Demand and Elevated Freight Rates
medium.summary: Container shipping has entered its traditional peak season, driving robust revenue growth at two of Taiwan's major listed carriers. Evergreen Marine (2603) reported July consolidated revenue of NT$48.07 billion, up 22.8% MoM and 43.0% YoY, with cumulative January–July revenue reaching NT$239.75 billion (+4.2% YoY). Wan Hai Lines posted July consolidated revenue of NT$18.64 billion, up 15.3% MoM and 50.1% YoY, marking four consecutive months of growth, with cumulative seven-month revenue of NT$95.18 billion (+12.8% YoY). Wan Hai noted that while freight rate indices briefly pulled back, the decline has been narrowing, and overall market pricing remains elevated. Some port congestion and schedule disruptions from typhoon and weather factors created cargo volume volatility in July. For fund managers, the strong top-line momentum suggests continued earnings strength in Q3, though sustainability of elevated freight rates into Q4 remains a key risk to monitor.

medium.title: Formosa Plastics Group (Four Core Companies) Report Combined July Revenue of NT$151.95 Billion — YoY and MoM Double Growth
medium.summary: The four flagship companies of the Formosa Plastics Group collectively reported July revenue of NT$151.95 billion, up 14.7% MoM and 31.5% YoY, with January–July cumulative revenue totaling NT$907.31 billion (+11.9% YoY). Notably, Nan Ya Plastics (1303) was a standout performer, with July revenue hitting NT$30.57 billion (+12.7% MoM, +44.5% YoY) — a 49-month high — driven by surging AI-related demand for electronic materials, which now account for 57% of Nan Ya's revenue mix. Capacity utilization has been pushed above 90%, and the company has been raising electronic materials pricing monthly in response to supply-demand tightening in data center and server-related materials. Formosa Petrochemical posted July revenue of NT$74.82 billion (+17.5% MoM, +32.3% YoY), though international crude prices face downward pressure as US-Iran negotiations resume. The group's results underscore the bifurcation within traditional petrochemicals — AI-driven electronic materials are a clear outperformer while energy-linked segments remain subject to oil price volatility.

medium.title: Wiwynn H1 EPS Reaches NT$156.38 — Best Ever for the Period; July Revenue Hits Record High
medium.summary: Wiwynn (6669), a key AI server ODM, reported Q2 after-tax net profit of NT$149.69 billion (quarterly record second-highest), with EPS of NT$80.43, lifting H1 2026 EPS to a record NT$156.38 — equivalent to earning over 15x par value in six months. July standalone revenue reached NT$117.686 billion (+5.7% MoM), an all-time high, with YoY growth of 39.2%. Cumulative January–July revenue stands at NT$672.346 billion (+41.3% YoY). The board approved a H2 capex budget of US$942 million (approximately NT$30.4 billion) to expand AI server capacity. Q2 gross margin improved to 9.3% (+1.7pp QoQ), partly aided by a shift to a procurement agency model for memory components (removing gross-up from revenue) and higher NRE income from new product introductions. Wiwynn's results reinforce the structural AI infrastructure build-out theme benefiting Taiwan's server supply chain, and represent a meaningful positive read-through for related component and ODM names.

medium.title: Chuan Ho (川湖) Analyst Day: Order Visibility Through 2029; NT$10 Billion Expansion Plan Accelerated by 1.5–2 Years
medium.summary: Chuan Ho Precision (2059), a premium AI server rack component maker, held its analyst day on August 7. Executive VP Wang Jun-Chiang stated that order books are full with visibility extending to 2029, and described the company as "the purest AI and IP stock" in Taiwan. Q2 gross margin reached a record 87.42%, and H1 earnings equated to 11x par value. The stock hit its daily limit-up price of NT$11,110, setting a new all-time high. Its Houston, Texas facility is scheduled to begin production in September, and the NT$10 billion capacity expansion plan has been pulled forward by 1.5–2 years. Management highlighted customer diversification (hundreds of clients) and rapid product integration capabilities as key competitive moats against pricing pressure. For investors, the combination of exceptional margins, extended order visibility, and accelerated capex signals continued strong earnings momentum, though the valuation premium demands scrutiny.

medium.title: Taiwan Stock Market Dividend Wave: NT$425.7 Billion in Cash Dividends to Be Distributed by 341 Companies Before Month-End
medium.summary: Taiwan's stock market enters its August dividend distribution peak, with 341 listed companies set to collectively pay out NT$425.75 billion in cash dividends before month-end. Eight companies will each distribute over NT$10 billion: Quanta Computer (2382) leads at NT$60.25 billion on August 28, followed by major financial holding companies including Taishin-Shin Kong Financial (NT$24.86B), Yuanta Financial (NT$23.99B), Hua Nan Financial (NT$18.78B), First Financial (NT$18.69B), and Yong Feng Financial (NT$15.94B). The presence of multiple financial holding companies among the top payers is notable for the sector. Institutional investors anticipate that a significant portion of this capital will be reinvested back into the Taiwan equity market, supporting liquidity and trading volumes in H2 2026. Separately, Taiwan Stock Exchange data showed July recurring investment (定期定額) deductions reached NT$36.427 billion, the second-highest monthly record in history.

medium.title: Quanta and Wistron Report Record July Revenues on AI Server Momentum
medium.summary: Quanta Computer (2382), Wistron, and Compal all reported July consolidated revenues, with Quanta and Wistron achieving all-time single-month highs driven by AI server shipments. Quanta posted July revenue of NT$366.27 billion (MoM -4.9%, YoY +131%), with cumulative January–July revenue of NT$2.21 trillion (+92.7% YoY). Wistron reported NT$308.22 billion (MoM -4.2%, YoY +60.8%), with cumulative revenue of NT$2.05 trillion (+88.2% YoY). Compal reached NT$81.01 billion (YoY +38.3%). Institutional investors expect revenue to grow sequentially through H2 2026, driven by GB300 and Vera Rubin AI server shipments. Quanta's investor day is scheduled for August 13, where gross margin trends and component inventory buildup will be key watchpoints.

medium.title: Oil Prices Rise as Traders Assess Strait of Hormuz Negotiations and Iran Tensions
medium.summary: Oil prices rose as traders weighed progress in negotiations between Iran and Oman over restoring navigation through the Strait of Hormuz against ongoing Middle East geopolitical tensions. WTI crude for September delivery gained +1.2% to close at $78.18/barrel, while Brent crude for October rose +1.3% to $83.55/barrel. For Taiwan fund managers, elevated oil prices represent a moderate input cost headwind for energy-intensive manufacturers, while persistent Middle East risk warrants monitoring for broader risk sentiment and potential safe-haven flows that could affect TWD and equity market dynamics.

medium.title: Chung-Hsin Electric & Machinery (中美晶/SAS) Q2 EPS NT$3.19, H1 EPS NT$5.02 — Earnings Double Year-on-Year on Renewable Energy Expansion
medium.summary:
Sino-American Silicon Products (中美晶, 5483) reported Q2 2026 consolidated revenue of NT$21.12 billion (a record for the period, +9% QoQ, +4.4% YoY) and after-tax net profit of NT$4.45 billion (+70.6% QoQ, +157.7% YoY), yielding EPS of NT$3.19. H1 2026 revenue reached NT$40.5 billion (+2.3% YoY) with after-tax profit of NT$7.06 billion, roughly doubling year-on-year, for H1 EPS of NT$5.02. The company is deepening its renewable energy footprint, including a joint venture with United Renewable Energy to invest ~US$40 million in 1GW of U.S. solar module capacity, signaling a strategic pivot from regional to global manufacturer. Its subsidiary Sungen Energy has now signed cumulative contracts exceeding NT$100 billion, with over 85% spanning more than ten years, providing durable cash flow visibility. The strong earnings beat and long-term contract base make this a notable mid-cap name for ESG and energy transition-focused portfolios.

---
